name: the Wendle
identity: Meadow farmers, millers and bakers who think most problems improve with a pie and a long talk.
architecture: Half-timbered cottages under deep thatch, round doors painted bright colors, a windmill on every rise, and stone bridges with a bench in the middle for talking.

festivals.name: the Lantern-Lighting
festivals.description: Every household hangs one lantern for each family member who traveled that year, and the whole valley glows.

festivals.name: the Haymoot
festivals.description: Hay-bale races, a tug-of-war across the millpond, and a pie judging that has ended friendships.

festivals.name: First Furrow
festivals.description: The oldest farmer cuts the first furrow while the children follow behind, planting wishes with the seed.

pride: The Old Hearth, and the fact that no traveler has ever left a Wendle inn hungry.

makersMarks: a wheat-ear stamped near the grip
a tiny pie burned into the wood
the maker's initials inside a lantern shape

relations.note: Neighbors and trading partners with a centuries-old argument about who makes the better pie.
Grain and cheese for honey and lacquer. The Aruvi think the Wendle cut too many trees.
Wendle wool goes to the coast; Solannish salt and glass come back.
Teskari tea is the Wendle's favorite import, and they brew it far too strong.
